label: OPTIMISE T2-02: statin for 10-year risk of 10% or more
title: No statin when the 10-year heart and blood vessel risk is 10% or more
statement: Consider statin therapy (eg. Atorvastatin 20 mg daily) for those adults who have ≥ 10% 10-year risk of developing CV disease using a validated CV risk assessment tool

source.document: Carolan A, et al. OPTIMISE. BMC Psychiatry 2022;22:585, Tables 2-3

plain_summary: For an adult with severe mental illness and no recorded statin supply, consider a statin if a validated tool gives a 10-year cardiovascular risk of at least 10%. An Australian five-year score cannot establish this threshold. Australian guidance differs: for eligible primary prevention patients, lipid-lowering treatment is recommended at five-year risk of 10% or more and considered at 5% to below 10%, with severe mental illness a reason to consider a higher risk category near a threshold (Australian CVD Risk Guideline, 2023).

medicine_groups.name: Statins (cholesterol-lowering medicines)
medicine_groups.note: Atozet is atorvastatin with ezetimibe. Rosuzet is rosuvastatin with ezetimibe. Vytorin is simvastatin with ezetimibe. Caduet is amlodipine with atorvastatin. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too. Ezetimibe on its own is not a statin.

medicine_groups.name: Antipsychotics and lithium (a sign the person may have severe mental illness)
medicine_groups.note: This group is not the medicine the finding is about. It only shows that the person may be in the group the OPTIMISE tool was written for. A medicine used for another reason, for example low-dose quetiapine for sleep, can mislead.

needs_facts.what: 10-year cardiovascular risk (percentage and name of validated tool)
needs_facts.meets: A recorded 10-year risk of 10% or more
A diagnosis of severe mental illness is documented.

rule_for_models: If severe mental illness is explicitly ruled out, give no finding. Use the most recent identifiable validated 10-year risk score. A score below 10% rules out a finding for that assessment. For people aged 18 or over with documented severe mental illness or a Group B supply suggesting it and no Group A statin supply anywhere in the history, report a full finding if the diagnosis is documented and that score is at least 10%. Cite the diagnosis and that score. If evidence needed for the finding is missing or uncertain, report a possible finding naming each missing or uncertain item (diagnosis, 10-year result or validated tool). A five-year score cannot establish the 10-year result. If age is unknown and the other evidence could meet this criterion, report at most a possible finding and ask the pharmacist to confirm whether the person is aged 18 or over.
cannot_be_seen: The risk score itself if no one recorded it, and the tool used. Smoking, blood pressure and cholesterol values. Past statin intolerance, a decision by the person to decline a statin, and statins supplied by a hospital or another pharmacy. Ask whether the person has been diagnosed with a severe mental illness, takes a statin from another pharmacy, or previously declined or could not tolerate one. Ask whether their doctor assessed cardiovascular risk and whether the result and tool are available.
ask_the_gp: Whether a statin should be started, after a review of the person's cardiovascular risk and any reason not to use one.
